items.description: Maintainer-only. Classifies every file that would newly ship to adopters against the written distribution-boundary categories, withholds by default when none matches cleanly, and asks the maintainer only where the taxonomy does not settle it, so the release CLI can produce a manifest.

items.name: /gaia-cleanse
items.description: Cleanses memory and auto-loaded files (CLAUDE.md, rules) of duplication with the wiki, contradictions with the wiki, and stale content, then asks one Apply / Discuss / Decline question; on Apply it applies the report, files any out-of-scope problem as a tech-debt issue, then commits, opens a PR, and merges it on a main-branch run like /update-deps. Pass --apply to re-run the apply-and-publish stage against the most recent report. Use when the user asks to cleanse or clean up memory, CLAUDE.md, or rules for duplication, contradictions with the wiki, or stale instructions. For duplication or broken links inside the wiki itself, use /gaia-wiki instead.

items.name: /gaia-codify
items.description: Drafts a guard (deterministic check, skill, or path-scoped rule) for a recurring code-audit finding class, with approval. Reviews recurring Code Audit Team findings and drafts the lowest-context-weight form into the working tree.

items.name: /gaia-debt
items.description: Fixes the tech-debt backlog, a single issue or a recommended related batch, highest severity then oldest first, on a fresh isolated branch through the audit gate, closing the issue(s) on merge. With no argument it drains the top of the backlog; one issue number fixes that issue directly, and several issue numbers name the operator's own batch, budgeted. An optional trailing `[use] worktree|branch` picks the isolation mode. A named number that cannot be drained stops with a reason. Use when the user asks to drain, fix, or work the tech-debt backlog or a named tech-debt issue.

items.name: /gaia-fitness
items.description: Lints this project's Claude integration (skills, commands, agents, rules, hooks, settings, CLAUDE.md files, wiki) with a deterministic rule catalog and reports an F-to-A+ grade, plus Claude Code built-in results and an advisory model judgment of descriptions, trigger overlap, rule scope and terminology. Proposes fixes for project-owned files only and applies each one only on a per-file yes, then offers to publish. Use when the user asks to check, grade or tidy their Claude setup.

items.name: /gaia-forensics
items.description: Turns a GAIA workflow misfire into a redacted, classified, filing-ready bug report in one read-only pass. Self-diagnoses config issues inline and files probable bugs upstream on confirmation.

items.name: /gaia-init
items.description: Initializes a new project from the GAIA harness. Renames, strips GAIA branding, configures i18n, and installs Claude skills and plugins.

items.name: /gaia-plan
items.description: Plans a complex feature with GAIA's task-orchestration pattern, structuring the work into fresh-context subagent phases for approval. Does not implement. Use when the user asks to plan a feature, break work into phases, or turn a SPEC into an execution plan.

items.name: /gaia-release
items.description: Maintainer-only. Cuts a new GAIA release. Bumps the version, graduates the CHANGELOG, regenerates the manifest, opens the release PR, then tags on merge.

items.name: /gaia-residue
items.description: Triages the keyed audit residue recorded in merged pull-request bodies. Enumerates candidates, resolves each one's cited line, and takes one disposition per entry (promote to a tech-debt issue, dismiss, or keep). Never fixes anything.

items.name: /gaia-spec
items.description: Authors an immutable SPEC artifact through Socratic discovery, then plans it in the same session and stops at the plan's KICKOFF prompt; execution starts in a fresh session. Pass `auto` before the description for a non-interactive mode that answers its own questions. Use when the user asks to write a spec, specify a feature, or pin down requirements before planning. Pass `reopen SPEC-NNN` to reopen a saved SPEC whose UAT cannot hold.

items.name: /setup-gaia
items.description: Runs the single post-init onboarding. Detects the situation and runs only the owed phases; safe to re-run. --reconfigure re-asks the sandbox (an admin's answer also sets the team sandbox-recommendation, asked on its own only when that answer cannot), isolation-policy, squash-only-merge, and statusline decisions.

items.name: cleanse
items.description: Cleanse memory and auto-loaded files (CLAUDE.md, rules): duplication across stores and with the wiki, contradictions with the wiki, promotable memory, stale entries, and auto-load bloat. The store listing, counts, budgets and dead-path signals come from the `gaia fitness` CLI; the model judges only what a script cannot. Conflicts between two committed instruction files are not judged here: `/doctor prompt-audit` owns them.

items.name: cleanse/apply
items.description: The Stage 2 procedure: apply the report's actions mechanically, verify they landed, file out-of-scope findings, finalize the report. Read whole by the Stage 2 subagent (the entry file's dispatch block says so).

items.name: cleanse/publish
items.description: Runs in the **main conversation** after Stage 2 returns, on any finalizing path (gated Apply, 0-action auto-apply, `--apply`). It never runs on Decline.

items.name: cleanse/research
items.description: The Stage 1 procedure and the report schema Stage 2 parses. Read whole by the Stage 1 subagent (the entry file's dispatch block says so). Audit the knowledge stores for duplication, stale entries, and auto-load bloat. **Wiki is the source of truth.** Memory is machine-local only. Auto-loaded files carry a token cost every session, keep them as pointers, push detail behind lazy wikilinks.

items.name: cleanse/verification-round
items.description: An adversarial verification round that hardens Stage 1's classifications against ground truth in the MAIN CONVERSATION, between Stage 1 returning its draft report and the Apply / Discuss / Decline decision gate. Stage 1's DUPLICATE / STALE / CONFLICT / PROMOTE / shrink classifications are single-pass semantic judgments that nothing else verifies before they drive edits, and for memory entries those edits are IRREVERSIBLE (machine-local under `$HOME/.claude`, no git undo). The round verifies the checkable claim behind each action against the actual stores, wiki, and repo, then drops, corrects, or re-spawns to harden the report before any human approval or any apply path consumes it.

items.name: codify
items.description: Human-gated codifying for the policy-memory loop. `/gaia-codify` is the ONLY code path that authors or activates anything in this loop, and it runs only under explicit human invocation. For each recurring finding it judges the lowest-context-weight form that fits, checks edit-vs-new first, and recommends exactly one action with rationale. It explains every item in plain language, presents the whole recommended plan once, and asks the human to accept it, change some items, or stop. Nothing is authored or activated unattended.

items.name: cost-record
items.description: Shared run-end cost record for the interactive GAIA command skills. A skill applies it from its own `## Cost record (run end)` section, substituting `{{COMMAND}}` with the command name (e.g. `gaia-debt`, `gaia-codify`). The skill keeps its own `## Cost record (run end)` heading and its run-ending-paths bullets inline (those are command-specific and anchor the `(Run ends here; see \`## Cost record (run end)\`.)` callbacks); this reference owns only the record call and the reporting rules below.

items.name: debt
items.description: Fix the `tech-debt` backlog the audit files. `/gaia-debt` reads the open `tech-debt` issues, orders them deterministically (highest severity then oldest first, no model call), recommends the top candidate, and resolves **one fix unit** per invocation, a single issue, a user-approved related batch of issues, or a batch the operator names by number, on a fresh branch through the same Code Audit Team marker gate every feature PR passes, with one `Closes #N` per member issue in the PR body so the merge closes every issue in the unit natively.

items.name: debt/named
items.description: The named-number procedures of `/gaia-debt`. `debt.md` routes here on every `numbers` result of its `## Argument parsing`, after its backlog read; every step after the pick returns to `debt.md`.

items.name: debt/recommend
items.description: The no-argument offer of `/gaia-debt`. `debt.md` routes here on a `top` parse after its backlog read, and `debt/named.md` routes here when the operator picks option 3 of the direct-number cluster offer.

items.name: debt/spec-handoff
items.description: The hand-off procedure for a confirmed spec-class member. `debt.md` routes here from its `## Fix-time spec screen`, once per confirmed member, including the members of a named set's spec hand-off. Do not implement a confirmed member; run these steps for it, then return to the spec screen's stop conditions in `debt.md`.

items.name: fitness
items.description: `/gaia-fitness` checks this project's Claude integration (skills, commands, agents, rules, hooks, settings, `CLAUDE.md` files, wiki) and reports an F-to-A+ grade. The CLI does the checking and the grading: `gaia fitness check` runs a fixed rule catalog over the files the project owns and prints one report. This playbook orchestrates around it: run the CLI and the Claude Code built-ins, dispatch one read-only judgment pass when there is anything to judge, render the card, heal only adopter files, one file at a time and each on a yes, verify with one re-run, and publish through a gate.

items.name: forensics

items.name: forensics/redaction

This file owns which lenses run and how their findings are applied.

items.name: plan/planner

You are a leaf subagent: do not dispatch subagents; parallelize investigation with parallel tool calls (batch reads and greps in one step), not sub-agent dispatch.

items.name: setup/github-repo
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 3 reads this file, whole, when the repo does not exist yet or its default branch is not pushed. Run `## Connect the repository` first; Options 1 and 2 return to `### Recommended defaults` in `setup-gaia.md`, and Option 3, the authentication refusal, and the clean-tree refusal skip the rest of Phase 3 and continue at Phase 3.5 in `setup-gaia.md`. items.name: setup/isolation-question

The calling command says what to do with a value and what no answer does.

items.name: setup/land-decisions
items.description: `/setup-gaia` reads this file, whole: Phase 5.5 runs `## Land the decisions` when project decisions may be recorded, and Phase 6 runs `## The setup ping` and then `## The closing message` on every run.

items.name: setup/migrate-2-machine
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 5 (`standalone-features.md`) runs this file for the `migrate-2-machine` feature. The 2.0.0 migration sets up only the machine that ran it; every other clone that was on GAIA 1.x carries 1.x leftovers until it catches up here, once, after pulling the merged migration. Run from the main checkout's root, never from a linked worktree (`/setup-gaia` already refuses one).

items.name: setup/per-machine
items.description: The four per-machine steps `/gaia-init` (Step 8) and `/setup-gaia` (Phase 2) share: external tools, Claude plugins, the statusline executable bit, and the app `.env`, plus the git hooks check (`## Git hooks`), which runs first on every read. Run from the repository root. The calling command says what a halt means for it and how to resume.

items.name: setup/sandbox
items.description: `/setup-gaia` Phase 2 reads this file, whole, and runs the part its sandbox route names. On `SANDBOX=ask` (`--reconfigure`, or a team recommendation and no marker), run the four steps below in order, then the honesty message on the enable path, then `## The admin's answer sets the team recommendation` on an answer. On `SANDBOX=stands`, run `## Record a settled decision` alone when `sandbox` is owed. On `SANDBOX=default-off`, run `## Default off` alone. Control then returns to Phase 2 of `setup-gaia.md`, which continues to Phase 3.

The calling command says what to do with a value and what no answer does.

Also trigger when the user asks about custom values, defining @theme tokens or CSS variables, naming color/spacing tokens, rem vs px, responsive breakpoints, or avoiding template literal class strings.

items.name: update-deps

items.name: .claude/skills/update-deps/references/override-audit.md
items.description: Each key in the top-level `overrides:` map in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` exists for one of two reasons: to resolve a **peer-dependency conflict**, or to enforce a **security floor** (pin a transitive dependency at or above a patched version to clear a known advisory). The two are detected by different tests, and an override is obsolete only when removing it regresses **neither**. A peer-dep test alone is blind to security-floor pins (a CVE pin never produces a peer-dep error), so it would wrongly delete every one of them.
